name: Bremen-Verden
alt: Duchy of Bremen and Principality of Verden

predecessors.name: Prince-Archbishopric of Bremen
predecessors.text: the Duchy of Bremen: the land between the Weser and the Elbe centred on Vörde and Stade, with Stedingen and the Land of Wursten

predecessors.name: Prince-Bishopric of Verden
predecessors.text: the Principality of Verden round Verden upon Aller

successors.name: Electorate of Hanover
successors.text: the same with Lehe and Bederkesa

ledger.x: 15 May 1648: the prince-archbishopric of Bremen is secularised as the hereditary Duchy of Bremen under the Swedish crown.
15 May 1648: the prince-bishopric of Verden becomes the Swedish Principality of Verden.
Early 1653: Swedish troops capture Lehe in the Swedish-Bremen war.
November 1654: the First Stade Recess cedes Lehe and Bederkesa.
November 1654: the First Stade Recess ends the Swedish-Bremen war; the Treaty of Habenhausen of 15 November 1666 ended a second one, with Sweden destroying its fortresses near Bremen.
1712: Denmark-Norway occupies the duchies in the Great Northern War.
1715: Denmark ends its occupation by selling the duchies to Hanover.
1715: Hanover takes de facto possession; Sweden has not yet ceded them.
1719: Sweden cedes the duchies to Hanover in the Treaty of Stockholm, which settled the war with Hanover; Hanover paid compensation 'of 1 million rixdollars'.

wars.name: Torstenson War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Brömsebro, 13 August 1645: Denmark-Norway ceded the occupied prince-bishoprics of Bremen and Verden into Swedish hands; the Peace of Westphalia secularised them in 1648.

wars.name: First Bremian War
wars.outcome: Sweden took Lehe in early 1653 and, in the First Stade Recess of November 1654, obtained Lehe and Bederkesa and tribute; Bremen's immediacy stayed unresolved and Sweden failed to take the city (Westphalia page: 'Swedish-Bremen wars of 1653/54').

wars.name: Great Northern War
wars.outcome: Denmark occupied the duchies in 1712 and sold them to Hanover in 1715; Sweden ceded them in the Treaty of Stockholm (1719) for a payment of 1 million rixdollars.

certainty.note: Drawn as circles round Stade, Stedingen, Wursten and Verden because the gazetteer lacks the Elbe-Weser district names; the page gives areas but no boundary.
